issue.title: Managed-tmp reaper fails every run on read-only (0555) test-vault dirs in agent-tmp and still reports ok
issue.description:
The age-horizon pass of the managed-tmp reaper removes directories with `fs::remove_dir_all` (sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/managed_tmp.rs` `remove_snapshot`). POSIX refuses to unlink entries inside a directory without owner write permission. Bob-cli test runs leave `bob-cli-complete-vault-<pid>-<ns>-<n>/vault` directories with mode 0555 and 0444 files inside agent TMPDIRs (`~/.cache/sase/tmp/agent-tmp/<launch key>/`). After the horizon expires, every such launch dir is selected and its removal fails, on every run.

Evidence on apollo, 2026-10-20 at sase 2648c7cdd and core b664b15b:
- The housekeeping `managed_tmp_reap` at 12:04:45 EDT reported `selected=198 removed=1 failed=197 ordinary_selected=198 ordinary_removed=1 ordinary_reclaimable_bytes=2237092017`, and `Structured job result: ok`. The failed count has been about 190-220 on every run in the retained log.
- `find ~/.cache/sase/tmp/agent-tmp -type d ! -writable` lists 295 directories, all `bob-cli-complete-vault-*/vault` with mode `dr-xr-xr-x`. 222 of the 261 agent-tmp entries contain one. agent-tmp totals 7.6 GB.
- Per-entry `removal_errors` are not logged by the chop, so the exact error string has not been seen. Confirm it first by logging or returning `removal_errors`. A dry-run `sase disk reap -j` cannot show it.

Fix:
1. In sase-core, before removing a tree the reaper owns, add owner write permission (u+w) to directories it owns. Do not follow symlinks, stay inside the managed root, and keep the existing fail-closed checks. A retry of `remove_dir_all` after the permission fix-up is enough.
2. Add a Rust test with a 0555 nested directory, then move sase's `sase-core-revision.txt` pin.
3. Surface removal failures: either log the first few `removal_errors` in the chop output, or make a nonzero `failed` produce a non-ok structured status. Today the job says `ok` with 197 failures.
4. Optionally, separately: the bob-cli test that builds the "complete vault" fixture should restore permissions on teardown. That lives in the bob-cli repo and is not required for this fix.

Related but different: sase-1bw (liveness incomplete because of SSH sessions) blocks the dead-launch pass, and this defect blocks the ordinary age pass. Both keep apollo's scratch from being reclaimed.

task_type_fields.impact: The ordinary age backstop never reclaims about 2.2 GB of stale agent TMPDIRs on apollo, which had 18 GB free after the 2026-10-20 ENOSPC, and the failure is invisible in structured job status.
task_type_fields.repro: On apollo: find ~/.cache/sase/tmp/agent-tmp -type d ! -writable lists 295 bob-cli-complete-vault-*/vault dirs (mode 0555). The housekeeping managed_tmp_reap logs selected=198 removed=1 failed=197 every hourly run, and the structured result is still ok.

issue.creation_reason: While triaging the athena/apollo operational log audit, apollo's housekeeping reaper was found to fail about 197 removals on every run. The cause is read-only test-vault directories that remove_dir_all cannot delete, and no existing bead tracks it.

payload.description: Same reaper, different blocker: sase-1bw keeps the dead-launch pass from reclaiming (liveness incomplete); this bead keeps the ordinary age pass from reclaiming (remove_dir_all fails)
sase-11h.3 owns propagation of cleanup-owner failures; managed_tmp_reap still reports ok with failed=197
